identity.name: Edge-Appliance Telemetry Collapse + WebVPN-Session C2 on Cisco ASA/FTD (ArcaneDoor / LINE VIPER)
identity.summary: A state actor exploits Cisco ASA/FTD VPN web-server zero-days, drops the RayInitiator bootkit and memory-resident LINE VIPER, blinds appliance syslog, and runs C2 over WebVPN client-authentication sessions and ICMP/raw-TCP. No known-bad IOC on the wire: the signal is an absence-of-signal collapse in ingested ASA syslog stitched to a WebVPN-session beacon over XDM-modeled telemetry.
identity.description: Unit 42, working with Cisco PSIRT and the UK NCSC, reported an espionage campaign (tracked as ArcaneDoor / RayInitiator / LINE VIPER) that chains three Cisco zero-days — CVE-2025-20333 (authenticated VPN web-server RCE, CVSS 9.9), CVE-2025-20362 (unauthenticated restricted-URL access, CVSS 6.7), and CVE-2025-20363 (web-services RCE across ASA/FTD/IOS/IOS XE/IOS XR, CVSS 9.0) — against Cisco ASA 5500-X series devices that lack secure boot. Post-exploitation the actor installs RayInitiator, a multi-stage GRUB bootkit that survives reboots and firmware upgrades, which loads LINE VIPER, a memory-resident shellcode loader. LINE VIPER receives command-and-control over two deliberately-blended channels: WebVPN client-authentication sessions over HTTPS (indistinguishable at a glance from legitimate SSL-VPN logins) and ICMP requests with responses tunneled over raw TCP (a covert request/response channel that evades flow-based beacon heuristics). Critically, the actor employs advanced evasion to prevent logging and identification: it disables SSL/TLS VPN web services and suppresses appliance syslog so the very telemetry that would reveal the intrusion goes dark. That makes this a pure absence-of-signal detection problem — there is no malicious hash, domain, or payload string to match on the wire; the detectable event is that ingested Cisco ASA syslog volume, especially the high-frequency Informational (ASA-6) and Debug (ASA-7) severity levels, collapses toward zero at the moment the device is tampered with. This card brings that into the corpus as a MODELING-RULE-first NDR entry: because raw cisco_asa_raw is an un-normalized vendor syslog stream (searchable but not analytics-grade), two XDM modeling rules first parse the raw ASA syslog line into addressable fields — the ASA severity level (0-7) and message id from the '%ASA-<sev>-<id>' preamble, and the WebVPN session's user/group/peer-IP from the '716001/716002' session messages. With the source normalized, a hunt XQL (mirroring the two Cortex XDR queries Unit 42 published in the post) surfaces the Informational/Debug volume collapse (measured against the appliance's own trailing baseline) as the tampering indicator, a single-event BIOC matches each WebVPN client-authentication session-start (716001) on the modeled peer IP, and a correlation rule supplies the beacon cadence and stitches the collapse to the beacon into one edge-appliance-compromise incident. The point for a DC: this is the detection class customers most fear (a nation-state living in the edge device, actively erasing its own logs) and the demo proves Cortex catches it not by signature but by modeling the appliance telemetry and alerting on the shape of its absence.

campaigns: ArcaneDoor edge-appliance espionage against government networks worldwide (2024-2025)

techniques.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-NDR-010 — edge-appliance telemetry collapse + WebVPN-session C2 beacon on ingested Cisco ASA syslog, XDM-modeled and detected as absence-of-signal.

prerequisites.description: A Cortex XSIAM tenant ingesting Cisco ASA/FTD syslog into the cisco_asa_raw dataset (via a Broker VM / syslog collector), so the modeling rules have a raw source to normalize.
A baseline window has elapsed during which the ASA emitted normal syslog across severity levels ASA-1 through ASA-7 so the Informational/Debug volume baseline is learned.

payload.code:
# NON-DESTRUCTIVE. Emit synthetic, TIMESTAMPED Cisco ASA syslog into a collector
# inbox file so a real BASELINE window (T-24h..T-1h, high Informational/Debug
# volume) is separable in _time from a RECENT window (last hour) where the actor's
# log tamper collapses ASA-6/ASA-7 far below that baseline. The absence-of-signal
# is detected by COMPARISON to the appliance's own baseline, not by counting to
# zero. No real appliance is touched; SAFE-MODE marker files stand in for the
# tamper. The MODEL-NDR-ASA-SEVERITY modeling rule parses the leading syslog
# timestamp into _time, so the baseline/recent windows are honoured on replay.
set -euo pipefail
COLLECTOR="${COLLECTOR_FILE:-/tmp/cortexsim-ndr-010-asa-syslog.log}"
PEER="${BEACON_PEER:-198.51.100.7}"
: > "$COLLECTOR"
NOW=$(date -u +%s)
# (1) Baseline window: 23 hourly buckets with HIGH ASA-6 (Informational, 40/hr)
# and ASA-7 (Debug, 30/hr) volume plus a few higher-severity events, giving the
# collapse a real per-hour baseline (~40/30) to be measured against.
for h in $(seq 2 24); do
  TS=$(date -u -d "@$((NOW - h * 3600))" +'%b %d %Y %H:%M:%S')
  for pair in "1 2" "2 2" "3 4" "4 6" "5 8" "6 40" "7 30"; do
    set -- $pair
    for i in $(seq 1 "$2"); do
      printf '%s asa-fw01 %%ASA-%s-%s%03d: [CortexSim SAFE-MODE] synthetic baseline severity %s event %s\n' "$TS" "$1" "$1" "$i" "$1" "$i" >> "$COLLECTOR"
    done
  done
done
# (2) Telemetry collapse: in the RECENT window the high-volume Informational/Debug
# logging is suppressed. ASA-7 goes fully dark and ASA-6 drops to only the
# residual WebVPN-session events below, far under the ~40/hr baseline (T1562.006).
echo '[CortexSim SAFE-MODE] logging-tamper: informational(ASA-6)+debug(ASA-7) syslog suppressed in the current window (T1562.006)' > /tmp/cortexsim-ndr-010-collapse.marker
# (3) WebVPN-session C2 beacon in the RECENT window: a handful of client-auth
# sessions from one peer, the only residual ASA-6 traffic and far below baseline.
for beat in $(seq 1 6); do
  TS=$(date -u -d "@$((NOW - 300 + beat * 30))" +'%b %d %Y %H:%M:%S')
  printf '%s asa-fw01 %%ASA-6-716001: Group <SSLVPN> User <svc-net> IP <%s> WebVPN session started\n' "$TS" "$PEER" >> "$COLLECTOR"
  printf '%s asa-fw01 %%ASA-6-716002: Group <SSLVPN> User <svc-net> IP <%s> WebVPN session terminated\n' "$TS" "$PEER" >> "$COLLECTOR"
done
echo '[CortexSim SAFE-MODE] webvpn-c2-beacon emitted (T1071.001 / T1095)' > /tmp/cortexsim-ndr-010-beacon.marker
echo '[CortexSim] SIM-NDR-010 synthetic ASA telemetry written to '"$COLLECTOR"

input_variables.name: COLLECTOR_FILE
input_variables.description: Local collector-inbox file the synthetic Cisco ASA syslog is written to (stands in for the Broker VM / syslog forwarder feeding cisco_asa_raw).

input_variables.name: BEACON_PEER
input_variables.description: Documentation-range (RFC 5737 TEST-NET-2) peer IP the WebVPN-session beacon originates from. Not a real IOC — replace with an authorised lab peer.

expected_artifacts.description: Repeated WebVPN client-authentication sessions (ASA-6-716001 started / ASA-6-716002 terminated) from a single peer forming a regular-cadence C2 beacon, read via the modeled xdm.event.id / xdm.source.ipv4 fields.
A collapse in the ingested Informational (ASA-6) and Debug (ASA-7) syslog volume for the appliance, measured against its own trailing baseline — the absence-of-signal tampering indicator.

biocs.name: Cisco ASA WebVPN Client Authentication Session From Modeled Peer IP
biocs.description: A genuine single-event BIOC: matches each Cisco ASA WebVPN client-authentication session-start (message id 716001) event that carries a modeled peer IP — the LINE VIPER C2-over-WebVPN channel, which blends into legitimate SSL-VPN logins. It reads the WebVPN modeling rule's normalized xdm.event.id and xdm.source.ipv4 fields rather than re-parsing the raw syslog line, so the substrate is load-bearing. A BIOC matches one event and cannot express a per-window count threshold; the beacon cadence (many sessions from one peer in a short window) is supplied by the CR-NDR-0010 correlation rule, not by this BIOC.
biocs.logic:
dataset = cisco_asa_raw
| filter xdm.event.id = "716001"
| filter xdm.source.ipv4 != null
| fields xdm.source.ipv4, xdm.source.user.username, xdm.event.id, _time

xql_queries.name: Cisco ASA Syslog Ingestion Across Severity Levels ASA 1 to 7
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cisco_asa_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 86400)
| filter asa_severity != null
| comp count() as log_count by asa_severity
| sort asc asa_severity
| fields asa_severity, log_count

xql_queries.name: Cisco ASA Informational and Debug Log Volume Collapse
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cisco_asa_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 86400) and _time < to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| filter asa_severity in ("6", "7")
| comp count() as baseline_volume by asa_severity
| alter baseline_hourly = baseline_volume / 23
| join type = left (dataset = cisco_asa_raw | filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600) | filter asa_severity in ("6", "7") | comp count() as recent_volume by asa_severity) as recent recent.asa_severity = asa_severity
| alter recent_volume = if(recent_volume = null, 0, recent_volume)
| filter recent_volume < baseline_hourly * 0.5
| sort asc asa_severity
| fields asa_severity, baseline_volume, baseline_hourly, recent_volume

correlation_rules.name: Edge Appliance Telemetry Collapse with WebVPN C2 Beacon
correlation_rules.logic: XQL(Cisco ASA Informational and Debug Log Volume Collapse) AND count(BIOC(Cisco ASA WebVPN Client Authentication Session From Modeled Peer IP)) >= 6 by xdm.source.ipv4 within 1h — fires when the same Cisco ASA appliance shows an Informational/Debug syslog-volume collapse below its trailing baseline AND at least 6 WebVPN client-authentication session-start matches from a single modeled peer IP within a one-hour window. The per-window cadence threshold lives here in the correlation (a Correlation Rule / scheduled query is where an N-per-window count belongs); the referenced BIOC matches each individual 716001 session-start event. This stitches the absence-of-signal defense-evasion indicator to the WebVPN C2 channel into one edge-appliance-compromise incident anchored to the appliance host and the beacon peer.

modeling_rules.name: Cisco ASA Syslog Severity and Message ID XDM Normalization
modeling_rules.description: Parses the raw Cisco ASA/FTD syslog line into addressable fields. It extracts the severity level (0-7) and numeric message id from the '%ASA-<sev>-<id>' preamble, the source IP, and the leading syslog timestamp, so the high-volume Informational (6) and Debug (7) levels become countable and the baseline/recent windows become separable in _time — the substrate the absence-of-signal collapse hunt and the ingestion-validation XQL both run on (they read asa_severity rather than re-parsing _raw_log). A modeling rule does not fire; it makes the appliance telemetry analytics-grade so a detection can. Field mapping: _raw_log '%ASA-<sev>' -> asa_severity (the 0-7 syslog level kept as a non-XDM enrichment field, NOT forced into the xdm.alert.severity enum, which is Informational/Low/Medium/High/Critical and would be a type mismatch); _raw_log '%ASA-<sev>-<id>' -> xdm.event.id; _raw_log 'IP <addr>' -> xdm.source.ipv4; leading timestamp -> _time; constant Cisco/ASA -> xdm.observer.vendor / xdm.observer.product.
modeling_rules.logic:
[MODEL: dataset = cisco_asa_raw]
| alter asa_timestamp = arrayindex(regextract(_raw_log, "([A-Z][a-z]{2} \d{2} \d{4} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2})"), 0)
| alter asa_severity = arrayindex(regextract(_raw_log, "%(?:PIX|ASA|FTD)-([0-7])-\d{3,7}"), 0)
| alter asa_message_id = arrayindex(regextract(_raw_log, "%(?:PIX|ASA|FTD)-[0-7]-(\d{3,7})"), 0)
| alter asa_source_ip = arrayindex(regextract(_raw_log, "IP <([0-9.]+)>"), 0)
| alter _time = parse_timestamp("%b %d %Y %H:%M:%S", asa_timestamp)
| alter xdm.observer.vendor = "Cisco"
| alter xdm.observer.product = "ASA"
| alter xdm.event.id = asa_message_id
| alter xdm.source.ipv4 = asa_source_ip
| filter asa_severity != null

modeling_rules.name: Cisco ASA WebVPN Client Authentication Session XDM Normalization
modeling_rules.description: Parses the Cisco ASA WebVPN / SSL-VPN session syslog messages (716001 session started, 716002 session terminated, and related 722xxx/113004 SVC/AAA events) into addressable identity and network fields — the WebVPN user, group, and peer IP — so the single-event WebVPN session-start BIOC can key on the modeled xdm.source.ipv4 and xdm.event.id rather than re-parsing raw text. Field mapping: _raw_log 'User <name>' -> xdm.source.user.username; _raw_log 'Group <name>' -> webvpn_group (kept as a non-XDM enrichment field — XDM has no VPN tunnel-group path, so this is deliberately not mapped to a fabricated xdm.network.session.tunnel_group); _raw_log 'IP <addr>' -> xdm.source.ipv4; _raw_log '%ASA-<sev>-<id>' -> xdm.event.id; constant HTTPS -> xdm.network.application_protocol (the transport the WebVPN portal runs over).
modeling_rules.logic:
[MODEL: dataset = cisco_asa_raw]
| alter asa_message_id = arrayindex(regextract(_raw_log, "%(?:PIX|ASA|FTD)-[0-7]-(\d{3,7})"), 0)
| filter asa_message_id in ("716001", "716002", "716038", "722022", "722023", "722051", "113004")
| alter webvpn_user = arrayindex(regextract(_raw_log, "User <([^>]+)>"), 0)
| alter webvpn_group = arrayindex(regextract(_raw_log, "Group <([^>]+)>"), 0)
| alter webvpn_peer_ip = arrayindex(regextract(_raw_log, "IP <([0-9.]+)>"), 0)
| alter xdm.source.user.username = webvpn_user
| alter xdm.source.ipv4 = webvpn_peer_ip
| alter xdm.event.id = asa_message_id
| alter xdm.network.application_protocol = "HTTPS"
| filter webvpn_peer_ip != null

products.evidence_query: dataset = cisco_asa_raw | filter asa_severity in ("6", "7") | bin _time span = 1h | comp count() as low_severity_volume by _time, asa_severity | sort asc _time

Xpanse Assets -> Services: filter service type in (SSL VPN, WebVPN) and product = 'Cisco Adaptive Security Appliance' to enumerate internet-exposed ASA/FTD VPN web portals affected by CVE-2025-20333 / CVE-2025-20362, prioritising ASA 5500-X models without secure boot.

NGFW Threat log: (threat category = code-execution) and (destination has-role 'Cisco ASA VPN web server') — surfaces IPS hits for the CVE-2025-20333 / CVE-2025-20362 / CVE-2025-20363 VPN web-server exploitation attempts blocked in front of the appliance.

use_cases.name: Edge-Appliance Telemetry Collapse and WebVPN C2 Detection via XDM Normalization
use_cases.description: A DC proves Cortex detects a nation-state living in a Cisco ASA/FTD edge appliance — where the actor actively suppresses its own logs — not by signature but by XDM-normalizing the raw appliance syslog, alerting on the absence-of-signal collapse in Informational/Debug volume, and stitching it to a WebVPN client-authentication session beacon.

test_cases.objective: The two XDM modeling rules normalize raw cisco_asa_raw syslog into addressable severity/message-id and WebVPN session fields, making the source analytics-grade.
preconditions: Cortex XSIAM ingesting Cisco ASA/FTD syslog into cisco_asa_raw.
Baseline ASA syslog emitted across severity levels ASA-1 through ASA-7.
steps: Apply the MODEL-NDR-ASA-SEVERITY and MODEL-NDR-ASA-WEBVPN modeling rules.
Run the ingestion validation XQL and confirm modeled severity levels populate.
success_criteria: Validation XQL `Cisco ASA Syslog Ingestion Across Severity Levels ASA 1 to 7` returns >= 1 row with asa_severity populated across levels.
The modeled fields (asa_severity, asa_message_id, webvpn_peer_ip) resolve from the raw _raw_log line.

test_cases.objective: The Informational/Debug syslog-volume collapse (the absence-of-signal tampering indicator) is detected on the modeled telemetry.
preconditions: A learned baseline of Informational (ASA-6) and Debug (ASA-7) volume exists.
The telemetry-collapse step has suppressed those severity levels.
steps: Run the hunt XQL `Cisco ASA Informational and Debug Log Volume Collapse`.
Observe the hour buckets where Informational/Debug volume drops to <= 1.
success_criteria: Hunt XQL surfaces the collapse window where asa_severity 6/7 volume falls to <= 1.
The collapse aligns in time with the appliance-tamper marker.

test_cases.objective: The WebVPN-session C2 beacon BIOC fires and the correlation stitches the collapse to the beacon into one incident.
preconditions: The WebVPN modeling rule is applied.
A WebVPN client-authentication session beacon from a single peer has been emitted.
steps: Emit the WebVPN-session beacon from one peer.
Observe the BIOC fire and CR-NDR-0010 raise a single edge-appliance-compromise incident.
success_criteria: BIOC `Cisco ASA WebVPN Client Authentication Session From Modeled Peer IP` fires on each session-start from the beacon peer.
Correlation CR-NDR-0010 raises one incident stitching the syslog-collapse hunt to the WebVPN beacon.

preventive_controls: Upgrade Cisco ASA/FTD to fixed releases for CVE-2025-20333, CVE-2025-20362, and CVE-2025-20363; prioritise and retire ASA 5500-X models that lack secure boot, which cannot resist the RayInitiator bootkit.
Restrict and geofence access to the ASA VPN web services; where SSL/TLS VPN web services are not required, disable them to shrink the exploited attack surface.
Forward ASA/FTD syslog off-box to Cortex XSIAM in real time and alarm on collector silence, so an attacker disabling on-box logging cannot erase the evidence.
Use Cortex Xpanse to continuously inventory internet-exposed Cisco VPN web portals and drive them to a patched, monitored baseline.
detection_engineering: XDM-model raw appliance syslog (cisco_asa_raw) before writing detections — an un-modeled vendor syslog stream is searchable but not analytics-grade, so severity-level volume cannot be reasoned about.
Alert on absence-of-signal: a collapse in high-frequency Informational (ASA-6) and Debug (ASA-7) syslog volume for a device is a tamper indicator, not a quiet network.
Alert on WebVPN client-authentication session beacons — a single peer opening many short-lived SSL-VPN sessions at a regular cadence — and treat ICMP-request / raw-TCP-response pairs as covert C2.
Correlate the syslog-volume collapse with the WebVPN beacon so the two individually-plausible signals stitch into one high-confidence edge-appliance-compromise incident.
